sections.h2: Which Athens County offices deal with property tax?
sections.html:
Two offices matter. The county auditor sets values and takes exemption applications at 15 S. Court Street in Athens, and its Real Estate Division answers at 740-592-3223. The county treasurer sends the bills and collects payment, including delinquent plans, escrow plans and mobile home tax.

The treasurer also chairs the county land bank, so a vacant or run-down house with back taxes can draw attention from that office as well as from a buyer.

sections.h2: What kind of housing market is Athens County?
sections.html:
Athens County sits in the hills of southeastern Ohio, 508 square miles of steep ridges and creek valleys drained mostly by the Hocking River. Athens is the county seat and largest city, and Nelsonville is the other city. Five school districts serve residents: Alexander Local, Athens City, Federal Hocking Local, Nelsonville-York City and Trimble Local.

  • Ohio University in Athens and Hocking College in Nelsonville anchor the economy, and more than a quarter of residents attend or work at one of them.
  • The 2020 census counted 62,431 people, with a median age of 29.5.
  • Of 26,386 housing units, 10.2% were vacant, and 45.6% of occupied homes were rented.

That high renter share means many sellers here own rental houses near campus, and rental owners should confirm each parcel's owner-occupancy status with the auditor before a sale.

sections.h2: When were Athens County's 2026 property taxes due?
sections.html:
The treasurer mailed real estate bills on January 30, 2026, and the first-half tax was due March 6, 2026. The treasurer's site later listed August 14, 2026 as a tax due date, with a note that penalties had been applied after it passed. Mobile home bills went out right after, with the same due date.

The treasurer states that Ohio law allows no grace period, so a payment received after the due date normally draws a penalty. Mailed checks are a risk because the Postal Service no longer postmarks the same day it receives mail. Paying online by electronic transfer carries a $0.50 fee, and payment plans exist for owners who call or visit the office.

Those 2026 dates are past, so for the next cycle read the due dates printed on the new bill. The statute behind them, ORC 323.12, sets the baseline of December 31 for the full amount or half then and half by June 20, and a mailed payment counts on its United States Postal Service postmark.

sections.h2: Why do values and tax bills differ so much between parts of Athens County?
sections.html:
The county mixes a university city, a former coal and salt district, and farm and forest land. Coal mining has fallen sharply from its peak, with one operator still working in Trimble Township, and quarries, oil and gas wells and the Wayne National Forest also use land here. Beef and dairy farms are the largest agricultural operations, and tourism is growing around the bike paths between Athens and Nelsonville.

Each of those uses can fall in a different school district and township, which changes the levies stacked on a parcel. Two houses of similar size in Athens and in Trimble can therefore carry different bills. Ask the auditor for the taxing district code on your parcel.

sections.h2: What is changing with the 2026 reappraisal?
sections.html:
Athens County's next countywide reappraisal is tax year 2026. New values took effect January 1, 2026 and first show on bills payable in 2027. The auditor posted preliminary values online and asks owners to check acreage, building size and construction details, then call the Real Estate Division about errors. Because the website shows only the new value, the auditor suggests comparing it against the second-half 2025 bill.

The auditor's site also summarizes several late-2025 state laws that limit automatic tax growth:

  • House Bill 186 adds an Inflation Cap Credit for certain school districts affected by the 20-mill floor, shown as its own line on the bill.
  • House Bill 335 limits growth in inside millage during valuation reset years to inflation.
  • House Bill 129 changes how the school district 20-mill floor is calculated, beginning with tax year 2026.

The auditor adds that these laws do not eliminate property taxes, repeal voted levies, reduce school bond millage or freeze values.

sections.h2: How do I dispute my Athens County valuation?
sections.html:
File a complaint with the county auditor, who presents it to the Board of Revision. Under ORC 5715.19(A)(1), the deadline is March 31 of the following tax year or the close of first-half collection, whichever comes later. The treasurer's own page lists the office as a member of the Board of Revision.

The same statute says the board must mail notice at least ten days before a hearing and decide within 180 days of the last filing day. While the case is pending, you may pay on the value you claim, and the treasurer must accept it. If you owe more at the end, interest runs on the shortfall. A parcel that had a complaint earlier in the same interim period needs a changed circumstance to file again, such as an arm's-length sale, casualty, a substantial improvement, or a fifteen percent shift in occupancy.

sections.h2: Which relief programs does the Athens County auditor describe?
sections.html:
Relief programs listed on the Athens County Auditor's FAQ
ProgramWho qualifiesHow to apply
Homestead exemptionAge 65 or older, or permanently and totally disabled, owning and living in the home on January 1; new applicants must also meet an income limit, stated as Ohio adjusted gross income under $38,600 for tax year 2024Mail the application to the auditor by December 31
Disabled veteran increaseVeterans with a 100 percent service-connected disability; exemption raised from $26,200 to $52,300Form DTE 105I
Owner occupancy reductionAny owner who lives in the home as principal residence on January 1, on one Ohio home per owner and spouseForm DTE 105C
CAUVFarmland of ten acres or more in exclusive agricultural use, or smaller tracts with at least $2,500 average yearly farm income over three yearsCall 740-592-3223

The income figure is tied to a stated tax year, so ask the auditor for the current limit before relying on it.

sections.h2: What should a seller do about taxes and the deed transfer?
sections.html:
Order a payoff from the treasurer before closing and confirm whether any plan balance is open. At transfer, the grantee files a statement of value with the auditor under ORC 319.202. It must record what the seller said about homestead or owner-occupancy reductions and about CAUV status, and a farm leaving CAUV can face a recoupment charge.

The auditor's conveyance fee under ORC 319.54(G)(3) is one dollar, or ten cents per hundred dollars or fraction of value, whichever is greater, paid by the grantor along with any county transfer tax under Chapter 322. Ask the Athens County auditor whether such a tax applies. Houses that are inherited, have tenants in place or need repairs can still close as-is, and the tax steps stay the same.

faqs.q: When were Athens County's 2026 real estate taxes due?
faqs.a: The treasurer's website lists March 6, 2026 for the bills mailed in January and August 14, 2026 as a later tax due date. Both dates have passed, so use the dates printed on your next bill.

faqs.q: Does the Athens County treasurer offer payment plans?
faqs.a: Yes. The treasurer says payment plans are available if you call or visit the office. An electronic payment option carries a $0.50 fee.

faqs.q: When does the new Athens County reappraisal show up on my bill?
faqs.a: On bills payable in 2027. The 2026 values took effect January 1, 2026, and preliminary values were posted on the auditor's website for owners to check.

faqs.q: Who qualifies for the Athens County homestead exemption?
faqs.a: Owners who live in the home on January 1 and are 65 or older or permanently and totally disabled, plus an income limit for new applicants. Applications go to the auditor by December 31.

faqs.q: How long do I have to challenge my valuation?
faqs.a: Until March 31 of the following tax year or the close of first-half collection, whichever is later, under ORC 5715.19(A)(1). File with the county auditor, who passes it to the Board of Revision.
